stem: Solve the compound inequality: -4 <= 2x - 6 <= 8. The solution set is:

per_option_rationale.rationale: Added -6 instead of +6 to the constant side: -4-6=-10, giving -5 <= x <= 1. Wrong direction of the shift.
Added 6 correctly (2 <= 2x <= 14) but forgot to divide by 2, giving 2 <= x <= 14, mistakenly reported as 1<=x<=14.
Left bound error: -4+6=2 divided by 2 gives 1, not -1. A sign slip on the left constant.

explanation: Add 6 to all three parts: 2 <= 2x <= 14. Divide by 2: 1 <= x <= 7. The key step is operating on all three parts of the compound inequality simultaneously.

explanation_sections.punchline: Compound inequalities are solved by applying the same arithmetic operation to all three parts.
explanation_sections.approach: Isolate x in the middle: add 6 throughout (-4+6=2, 8+6=14), then divide by 2 (positive, no flip). Result: 1 <= x <= 7.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always operate on ALL three parts of a compound inequality. Forgetting the middle or changing only one side corrupts the solution.
explanation_sections.timing: 60 s. Two arithmetic steps. Trap: sign error on the constant (option 2) or forgetting division (option 3).
